name: Zoe Costa

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI firms or campaigns. Your name stays confidential. What does a normal day look like for you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: At Harbour Ledger I open the marina suppliers' accounts, check bank entries against invoice pictures, then ring clients about gaps. I like the call where a worried owner finally sees the cash pattern; I hate copying a blurred photo into three screens.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How did you come to run the team?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm forty-three, with a master's degree and a chartered accountancy qualification, and I've worked through enough summer rushes to know where the mistakes hide. I lead four people, but I still check the returns before they go out; I use AI each day to draft questions, never to sign figures for me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau — Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell my team at Harbour Ledger that a modest tool is fine if it helps us find the duplicate invoice before the client does. I still want a person to own the final return.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I already use AI each day to draft the first list of questions for marina suppliers, and I check every figure myself. We have roughly four months of expenses saved and my pay is normal for a team lead, so a small time saving doesn't threaten our mortgage by itself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep my daily question draft and sign-off routine, then set aside fifty a month from salary for the children's school costs. I'd bring the duplicate-invoice tally to our Friday team meeting so the partners see what review still does.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about my own work in this picture. The household budget needs care, but my pay and my partner Luis's electrician wage are steady now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which part of your day do you like?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I like getting a marina owner to understand where the cash has gone after a busy summer. A clean set of accounts lets a worried marina owner sleep.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What frustrates you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Supplier invoices arrive as photographs with half the page cut off. Re-entering them is dull, and the machine is welcome if it catches the missing corner instead of guessing.

say: I'd welcome **duplicate-invoice checks** with a person signing the return.
I'd show partners **review errors** at the Friday meeting.
think: My daily AI drafts are already **checked by me**.
Four months saved and two wages make the **mortgage manageable** now.
do: Keep **daily drafted questions** and manual sign-off on marina supplier returns.
Save **fifty monthly** from my salary for the children's school costs.
Bring the **duplicate-invoice tally** to Friday’s team meeting.
feel: I feel **calm** about my current job.
S0.quote: A clean set of accounts lets a worried marina owner sleep.
fieldNote: Zoe already uses AI **daily** for question drafts; she maintains her checked routine in this scenario.
Four months saved and **two steady wages** make the baseline manageable, though school costs still matter.

steps.text: Keep daily AI-drafted client questions with manual figure sign-off
Save fifty monthly from salary for children's school costs
Bring duplicate-invoice tally to Friday team meeting

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption — Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask Harbour Ledger to publish how many supplier corrections the new software makes and misses. Clients should hear who is responsible before we promise a faster return.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'm quick with tools, but this could swallow the first pass and leave me supervising more files with fewer paid reviewers. The danger isn't that I can't click the buttons; it's that my own lead hours become a cheaper line in the budget.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the partner for a paid vendor session to learn the new invoice-matching controls on closed marina files, with our senior reviewer checking the errors. In the first year of steady change, if my paid lead hours fall, I'd apply for posted senior roles at the other firms nearby, retaining Harbour Ledger pay until a written offer gives a mortgage-covering wage and start date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about a cut to my own paid hours. Four months saved would buy time, but not a long job search with two children.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you put live invoices into the new tool?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only after the partner signs off the trial and access rules. If they refuse paid vendor time, I'll stay with our approved daily tools; I won't teach myself on live client records at night.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the senior reviewer check?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The invoice number, the image and the bank entry side by side. I'd count false matches, because a pretty dashboard can hide a very expensive wrong payment.

say: I'd publish **missed supplier corrections** alongside speed gains before promising clients faster returns.
I'd insist on **named responsibility** for each filed return.
think: Fewer reviewers could mean **fewer lead hours** for me.
Four months saved would not fund a **long search**.
do: Learn **invoice controls** in paid vendor time with senior error checks; use live only after partner-approved trial and access rules.
Apply for **posted senior roles** if my paid lead hours fall.
Keep **paid Harbour hours** until a written mortgage-covering offer starts.
feel: I feel **anxious** about losing paid hours.
S1.quote: I'd count false matches, because a pretty dashboard can hide a very expensive wrong payment.
fieldNote: Her new learning concerns **invoice-matching controls**, distinct from the daily drafting tool she already checks.
The outside search follows a **lead-hours cut**; she retains offered pay until posted work has written wage and start.

steps.text: Learn invoice controls on closed files in approved paid vendor session with senior error checks
Use live invoices only after partner signs trial and access rules
Keep approved daily tools if paid vendor trial refused
Apply to posted nearby senior roles after lead-hours cut; keep Harbour pay until written mortgage-covering wage/start

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028 — Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell marina clients that full AGI in 2028 can do almost all our tax reasoning and matching. Robots for the physical work at their yards come later, around 2031, so I won't claim a warehouse job is a safe escape.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect Harbour Ledger to shed much of its accounts team, possibly my post. Luis's electrician wages cover part of our mortgage, but losing my salary would still force us to draw down the four-month buffer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd postpone the family boat course and save its eighty monthly fee now. In the first year after 2028, if Harbour ends my job, I'd apply for advertised salaried credit-control roles at the local bank, keeping any paid firm closeout hours while offered until a written wage that covers our mortgage and a start date are confirmed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed because I expect a serious loss of my own earnings. The four-month buffer is useful, but it isn't enough to pretend a bank vacancy exists.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who gets the children after school if the bank shift runs late?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner Luis can collect them on his early-finish days. I would accept a bank shift only if its actual start and finish times fit the school run or he confirms the pickup days; I won't promise time he hasn't got.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the bank has no paid vacancy?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd take only any paid Harbour Ledger closeout hours still offered and use savings for essential bills. I'd keep looking at posted work, not offer the bank free trial days.

say: I'd explain that **2028 tax reasoning** changes before yard robots around 2031.
I'd avoid promising clients a **physical-work escape**.
think: I expect a **large salary loss** if the accounts team shrinks.
Luis's wage would cover only **part of our mortgage**.
do: Save **eighty monthly** by postponing the boat course.
Take **posted bank work** after layoff only with written mortgage-covering pay, start and shifts fitting school pickup or Luis’s confirmed days.
Keep **offered closeout hours**, use savings for essentials and continue searching if the bank has no vacancy.
feel: I feel **alarmed** about losing my salary.
S2.quote: The four-month buffer is useful, but it isn't enough to pretend a bank vacancy exists.
fieldNote: Her bank route needs a **real salaried vacancy**, written mortgage-covering wage and start, plus feasible school pickup.
The cancelled course adds **new cash**; Harbour closeout pay continues only while the firm offers it.

steps.text: Postpone family boat course and save eighty monthly
Take posted bank work after layoff with written mortgage-covering pay/start and confirmed pickup-compatible shifts
Keep offered closeout hours, use savings for essentials and search postings without bank vacancy

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031 — Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the partners that the extra years should be spent testing who pays for correcting bad records, not decorating a website with AI promises. Full AGI reaches our desk in 2031 and physical marina work faces robots around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I can move fast with software, but I don't own the client contracts. If the firm stops billing for checks, my ability to catch an error may have no paid slot.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep a monthly record of paid correction work and ask Harbour Ledger for a written staffing and fee plan each tax season. In the first year after 2031, if the firm cannot fund my lead salary from those fees, I'd apply for posted salaried bank credit-control work, keeping any paid Harbour hours until a written mortgage-covering wage, start date and school-compatible shift are confirmed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious because a good skill doesn't automatically produce a wage. The extra years give me time to learn where the bank's paid vacancies are, not a guarantee of one.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you pay for another credential?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have a master's degree and a chartered accountancy qualification. I'd take a required bank compliance module only if a real paid posting calls for it and the bank funds the fee and paid study hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the bank never advertises?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep paid Harbour work while it exists and ask the partners about wage-bearing correction roles. I wouldn't spend our school money on an unposted bank course.

say: I'd demand a **written fee plan** for human corrections.
I'd distinguish **2031 desk risk** from 2034 yard robots.
think: My skill matters only if **someone funds** the role.
A bank position is a **possible vacancy**, not promised income.
do: Record **paid correction fees** and request a written plan each tax season.
Take **funded bank compliance** only for a posted paid role.
Seek **posted bank work** if lead pay fails; require written mortgage pay, start and school-compatible shifts, retaining offered Harbour hours.
feel: I feel **anxious** about finding paid work.
S3.quote: I feel anxious because a good skill doesn't automatically produce a wage.
fieldNote: Her **monthly correction record** tests paid demand; without a bank vacancy, she retains offered Harbour work and asks about funded corrections.
The bank module needs **funded fees** and paid time for a posted paid role; a move needs written terms and school-compatible shifts.

steps.text: Log paid corrections monthly, request annual staffing plan; without bank vacancy request funded correction work
Take compliance module only for posted paid bank role with funded fee and paid study hours
Apply for posted bank credit-control if Harbour cannot fund lead salary
Keep available Harbour pay until written mortgage-covering wage/start and school-compatible shifts

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036 — Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say a decade gives us a chance to pay down the mortgage and see which corrections clients still buy. It doesn't make the accounts desk safe when full AGI arrives in 2036; physical robots follow around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 53 I might have older children, but I'd still need earnings. If Harbour's clients stop paying for a lead accountant, I won't treat a busy-looking dashboard as proof the salary is safe.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd add a hundred monthly from wages to our reserve while Luis and I both have full weeks, and review paid correction fees with the partner each year. In the first year after 2036, if Harbour cannot fund my lead salary, I'd apply for posted salaried bank credit-control work and keep available paid Harbour hours until a written mortgage-covering wage, start date and workable school pickup are confirmed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about losing a wage even with a decade's notice. Today's four-month buffer still has to carry the family if either income drops.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if Luis loses electrician shifts before 2036?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd pause the extra hundred and use both current wages for the mortgage and food. A savings target isn't worth an overdue loan bill.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you leave accounting now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. I like making sense of marina accounts and I'm paid for it today; I'd make the annual fee check before jumping to another employer.

say: I'd ask whether **paid correction fees** support a lead post.
I'd explain **2036 desk risk** before 2039 yard robots.
think: I still need a **salary at 53** to support the household.
A four-month buffer cannot replace **either wage** while the mortgage and school bills continue.
do: Save **one hundred monthly** while both wages hold; otherwise direct current wages to mortgage and food.
Check **paid correction fees** with the partner each year.
Apply for **posted bank work** if Harbour cannot fund my lead salary.
feel: I feel **anxious** about an earnings gap.
S4.quote: A savings target isn't worth an overdue loan bill.
fieldNote: Her ten-year preparation depends on **current wages**; added cash stops if Luis's electrician shifts fall.
Her 2036 search starts when Harbour cannot fund **lead salary**; she retains only offered work and requires written new-job terms.

steps.text: Save hundred monthly while wages hold; otherwise use current wages for mortgage and food
Review paid client correction fees with partner each year
Apply for posted bank credit-control if Harbour cannot fund lead salary
Keep available Harbour pay until written mortgage-covering wage/start and school pickup

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most, because a quick loss of my own salary would turn four months' savings into mortgage payments. An actual posted bank job with written pay, hours and a start date would help; a list of possible careers wouldn't.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who gets the children when a new shift begins. A paper offer can look excellent until the school gate closes before its finish time.

headlineQuote: A paper offer can look excellent until the school gate closes before its finish time.
portrait: Zoe is a **chartered team lead** who likes explaining marina accounts and dislikes copying blurred invoices.
She uses AI **daily** for draft questions but signs figures herself.
Typical pay, Luis's wage and **four months saved** support their mortgage and two children.
She tests **new invoice controls** only with approval, paid time and a senior reviewer.
AGI could remove her **lead salary**; any bank move needs written terms and school pickup.
biggestWorry: She worries most about **AGI by 2028** quickly ending her own lead salary.
whatWouldHelp: She wants a **posted paid bank role** with written wage, hours and start date that work with school pickup.
